beats.say: Windows XP arrived on retail shelves on 25 October 2001, changing computing forever.
Before you heard that legendary startup chime, Microsoft started development under the codename Whistler for home users.
Engineers built it by merging two separate internal efforts called Neptune and Odyssey into one system.
They chose the famous Bliss desktop wallpaper, which was an actual photograph of a landscape taken in California.
Manufacturing completed on 24 August 2001, just two months ahead of retail launch day for consumers.
Your family desktop suddenly gained a brighter interface, yet support lasted until 8 April 2014 for millions.
What happened next is in Part 2. Subscribe for one of these every day!

meta.summary: Windows XP officially arrived on retail shelves on 25 October 2001 after development under the codename Whistler. Here is how Microsoft built the operating system that shaped personal computing.
meta.comment: Did you use Windows XP on your very first family desktop?
sources: The Verge, Microsoft’s Windows XP Crocs are no joke, 2025-08-05
facts: Windows XP was released to retail on October 25 2001.
Windows XP was developed under the codename Whistler after merging the Neptune and Odyssey projects.
Windows XP’s default wallpaper is the Bliss image, a photograph of a landscape.
Windows XP was released to manufacturing on August 24 2001.
Extended support for Windows XP ended on April 8 2014.
